lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which file would you use to apply global styles to your entire React app?

App.cssHeader.cssindex.jsxindex.html

Make sure to pick App.css.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your app loads App.css, which contains a body rule. You rename the file to Theme.css.

Which change keeps the same page styling?

Update the import to load Theme.css; keep the body selector.Keep importing App.css; React automatically finds renamed CSS files.Update the import and change body to Theme to match the filename.Remove the import; a file named Theme.css applies automatically.

Update the import to load Theme.css; keep the body selector.

Add the correct CSS class to apply the defined rule from the UserProfile.css file.

Make sure to pick className, followed by =, and finally "userProfile".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make the outer div receive the border, padding, and background defined by the .userProfile selector.

Make sure to pick className, followed by =, and finally "userProfile".

lessons.title: Lesson #1 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the correct CSS class to the div to apply the defined CSS rule in Square.css.

Make sure to type "square".

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Do the two CSS rules in the App.css file make sense?

Yes, as they are general rules targeting elementsNo, they should move into a more specific CSS fileNo, we must not define any CSS rules in the App.css fileNo, as we should define general CSS rules in the index.css file

Yes, as they are general rules targeting elements.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Imagine changing the h1 selector in App.css to p, leaving everything else unchanged.

Which element loses its blue text rule, and which rule still applies?

The heading loses its blue text rule; the page background stays dark orange.The heading stays blue because the rule remains in App.css.The heading loses its blue text rule and the body loses its background rule.The heading becomes dark orange because the body rule changes its text color.

The heading loses its blue text rule; the page background stays dark orange.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Do we need to include the index.css file when using React even though we are not using it actively?

Yes, as the bundler requires this import statementNo, if we don't use it, we don't need itYes, but we should use itNo, including it would be a mistake

Yes, as the bundler requires this import statement.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your entry HTML already links to the existing index.css. You add a body background rule there.

What else is needed to load that rule when the page opens?

No new import; the existing stylesheet link loads the new rule.Import index.css in every component that renders an element.Rename the file to App.css because index.css cannot hold CSS rules.Replace the HTML link with a JavaScript import inside the CSS file.

No new import; the existing stylesheet link loads the new rule.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the correct property to apply inline styling to the div.

Make sure to pick style.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make this div render as the shown 100px blue square using its inline style object.

Make sure to pick style, followed by backgroundColor.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is true about how React handles the style property?

It uses a JavaScript object instead of a stringIt uses a string like HTMLIt always expects a single styling ruleStylings must be applied in a CSS file

It uses a JavaScript object instead of a string.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which JSX opening tag gives a button an inline red text color?

<button style={{ color: "red" }}><button style="color: red"><button style={color: "red"}><button class="color: red">

<button style={{ color: "red" }}>.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Check if the passed property size equals "small" to dynamically set the width and height of the div element.

Make sure to pick props.size, followed by ===.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make the box with size="small" use 40px, while every other size uses 120px.

The value after ? is used when the condition is true; the value after : is used otherwise.

Make sure to pick ===, followed by "small", "40px", and finally "120px".

lessons.title: Lesson #1 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's missing in the HTML code that is prohibiting the CSS from being rendered?

Importing the index.css file that the React bundler requiresNothing, the CSS is applied correctlyImporting the App componentImporting the App.css file

Importing the index.css file that the React bundler requires.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The copied App.jsx imports ./App.css, which sets an h1 background to red. What happens to the rendered Hi! heading?

It receives a red background.It stays unstyled because index.css is not linked.It disappears because CSS imports cannot be in components.The whole page becomes red, but not the heading.

It receives a red background.

lessons.title: Lesson #4

Given the following code, what will be the background color of all div elements?

YellowBlueRedGreen

Make sure to pick Yellow.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Imagine Header returns <section>Hello World</section>. Keep the HTML and CSS unchanged.

Which element still matches the div rule?

The root div in index.html, but not the new section.The new section, but not the root div.Both elements, because both belong to the React app.Neither element, because Header no longer returns a div.

The root div in index.html, but not the new section.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
If you want to apply styles only to the ProductList component, where should you import the ProductList.css file?

ProductList.jsxApp.cssApp.jsxindex.css

Make sure to pick ProductList.jsx.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You import ProductList.css in ProductList.jsx. It defines .product-card.

Another component also renders an element with className="product-card". Which elements can this rule style?

Matching elements from both components, because the CSS class selector is shared.Only ProductList elements, because that component imports the file.Only the other component, because ProductList is excluded by its own import.Neither component until the file is renamed App.css.

Matching elements from both components, because the CSS class selector is shared.

classidstylediv

classNameclassstyleid

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the styles variable describe?

A JavaScript object that defines stylesA CSS stylesheet fileA string of CSS rulesAn array of style names

A JavaScript object that defines styles.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The copied styles object sets backgroundColor to yellow and fontSize to 20px.

If a component uses style={styles}, which result should it have?

A yellow background and 20px text.A CSS file named styles is loaded.The text becomes yellow but the background stays unchanged.React treats the object as an array of class names.

A yellow background and 20px text.

What property is used to apply custom styles to a React component?

styleclassiddata

Make sure to pick style.
lessons.hardModeContent:
React uses the style property to apply custom styles to a component.

Given const cardStyles = { color: "navy" };, which JSX uses that object?

<section style={cardStyles}><section class={cardStyles}><section id={cardStyles}><section data={cardStyles}>

<section style={cardStyles}>.
